What is a whole number?

Good question! Whole numbers are the counting numbers we use every day, like 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 and so on. They have no parts and no pieces, so there is no half and no fraction. When you count the oranges in a basket or the pupils in your class, you are using whole numbers. For example, if there are 35 pupils in your class, 35 is a whole number. We can keep counting bigger and bigger, all the way up to one million and beyond. You are doing very well!

How do I count in thousands up to one million?

Well done for asking! To count in thousands, you add 1,000 each time. Start like this: 1,000, then 2,000, then 3,000, and keep going. After 999,000 the next number is 1,000,000, which we call one million. One million is a 1 followed by six zeros. Think of it like counting bags of rice in a very big store, where each bag holds one thousand grains. Counting in thousands helps you reach big numbers quickly. Keep practising and you will count to one million with ease!

Can you teach me to count in fives?

Of course! Counting in fives means you add 5 each time. It goes like this: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50. Do you see the pattern? Every number ends in 5 or 0. This is very useful in real life. Imagine you are selling oranges in groups of five for your mother in the market. You count 5, 10, 15, 20 to know how many you have sold. Counting in fives is fast and easy. Try it with your fingers and you will soon be an expert!

How do I count in sevens?

Great effort! Counting in sevens means you add 7 each time. Start at 7, then 14, then 21, 28, 35, 42, 49, 56, 63, 70. Here is a helpful example: there are 7 days in one week. So after 1 week you have 7 days, after 2 weeks you have 14 days, and after 3 weeks you have 21 days. Counting in sevens helps you work out days quickly. It may feel tricky at first, but with a little practice you will count in sevens smoothly. Keep going, you are learning fast!

What does counting in twelves mean?

Nice question! Counting in twelves means you add 12 each time: 12, 24, 36, 48, 60, 72, 84, 96, 108, 120. We call a group of twelve a dozen. So one dozen eggs is 12 eggs. If your aunty buys 2 dozen eggs for her shop, that is 24 eggs. Three dozen would be 36 eggs. Counting in twelves is useful when you buy things in dozens, like eggs, pencils or biscuits. Practise saying the numbers out loud, and counting in twelves will become very easy for you!

Why do we count in sixties?

Good thinking! We count in sixties because of time. There are 60 seconds in one minute and 60 minutes in one hour. So counting in sixties goes like this: 60, 120, 180, 240, 300. For example, 60 seconds make 1 minute, 120 seconds make 2 minutes, and 180 seconds make 3 minutes. This helps you understand the clock on the wall. When you know how to count in sixties, you can change seconds into minutes very fast. Keep practising with a clock at home and you will get better and better!

How do I change seconds into minutes?

Well done for asking! To change seconds into minutes, you divide the number of seconds by 60, because 60 seconds make 1 minute. For example, let us change 180 seconds into minutes. We divide 180 by 60, which gives us 3. So 180 seconds is the same as 3 minutes. Here is another one: 120 seconds divided by 60 gives 2, so that is 2 minutes. Think of waiting 120 seconds for your noodles to cook, which is just 2 minutes. You are understanding time very well, keep it up!

How many minutes make an hour, and how do I change minutes to hours?

Great question! There are 60 minutes in 1 hour. To change minutes into hours, you divide the minutes by 60. For example, let us change 120 minutes into hours. We divide 120 by 60 and get 2, so 120 minutes is 2 hours. Another example: 180 minutes divided by 60 gives 3, so that is 3 hours. Think about a football match in Lagos that lasts 90 minutes, which is one and a half hours. Knowing this helps you read time and plan your day. You are doing a wonderful job!

Can you explain place value to a Primary 4 pupil?

Good question! Place value tells us how much each digit in a number is worth, based on where it stands. In the number 4,572, look at each digit from the right. The 2 is in the units place, the 7 is in the tens place, the 5 is in the hundreds place, and the 4 is in the thousands place. So 4,572 means 4 thousands, 5 hundreds, 7 tens and 2 units. Place value is like giving each digit a special seat. Once you know the seats, big numbers become easy. Keep practising and you will master it!

What is the place value of each digit in 36,148?

Well done for trying a big number! In 36,148 we read the digits from the right. The 8 is in the units place, so it is worth 8. The 4 is in the tens place, worth 40. The 1 is in the hundreds place, worth 100. The 6 is in the thousands place, worth 6,000. The 3 is in the ten thousands place, worth 30,000. So the number is 30,000 + 6,000 + 100 + 40 + 8. Breaking a number apart like this helps you see its true size. You are doing great work!

How do I write the number 250,000 in words?

Great question! To write a number in words, we use the place values to guide us. The number 250,000 has a 2 in the hundred thousands place and a 5 in the ten thousands place. So we read it as two hundred and fifty thousand. Imagine a new car in Abuja costing two hundred and fifty thousand naira. Reading big numbers in words helps everyone understand prices and amounts clearly. Always start from the left and read each group. You are learning to handle big numbers very nicely, keep it up!

What are Roman numerals?

Nice question! Roman numerals are special letters that the ancient Romans used to write numbers, and we still see them today on some clocks and books. The main ones are: I means 1, V means 5, X means 10, L means 50, C means 100, D means 500, and M means 1000. For example, the number 3 is written as III, and the number 8 is written as VIII. You may see Roman numerals on a clock face or on the pages at the front of a textbook. Learning them is fun, so keep practising!

How do I write 1000 and other big numbers in Roman numerals?

Well done for asking! In Roman numerals, the letter M stands for 1000. So one thousand is simply written as M. Let us look at a few more. The number 100 is C, 500 is D, and 1000 is M. To write 1500, we put M and D together to get MD, because 1000 + 500 is 1500. To write 2000, we write MM, because that is 1000 + 1000. Roman numerals add the letters together to make the number. Take your time with them and you will write big numbers like a champion!

What is the LCM of 12 and 18?

Great question! LCM means Lowest Common Multiple. It is the smallest number that both numbers can divide into evenly. Let us list the multiples. Multiples of 12 are 12, 24, 36, 48. Multiples of 18 are 18, 36, 54. Look carefully: the smallest number that appears in both lists is 36. So the LCM of 12 and 18 is 36. Think of two friends in Kano, one clapping every 12 seconds and one every 18 seconds; they clap together again after 36 seconds. You worked through that beautifully, keep it up!

How do I find the HCF of 24 and 36?

Well done for asking! HCF means Highest Common Factor. It is the biggest number that can divide both numbers evenly. First we list the factors. Factors of 24 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. Factors of 36 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. Now look for the common ones: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12. The biggest common factor is 12. So the HCF of 24 and 36 is 12. Finding factors carefully is the secret. You are doing excellent work!

Find the missing number: 5, 10, 15, __, 25.

Good thinking! To find the missing number, we look for the pattern. Let us check how the numbers change. From 5 to 10 we add 5. From 10 to 15 we also add 5. So the rule is to add 5 each time. That means after 15 we add 5 again, which gives us 20. We can check: 20 plus 5 gives 25, which matches the last number. So the missing number is 20. This kind of puzzle is called quantitative aptitude, and finding the pattern is the trick. You solved it very well, bravo!

Arrange these numbers from smallest to biggest: 4,512, 4,215, 4,125.

Great question! To arrange numbers, we compare them using place value, starting from the left. All three numbers begin with 4 thousands, so we look at the next digit, the hundreds. We have 5 hundreds, 2 hundreds and 1 hundred. The smallest hundreds digit is 1, then 2, then 5. So the order from smallest to biggest is 4,125, then 4,215, then 4,512. Comparing big numbers is like lining up pupils by height in your class. Always start from the left. You are getting very good at this, keep practising!

Why are whole numbers useful in everyday life in Nigeria?

Lovely question! Whole numbers help us in so many everyday ways. When your mother counts the change in naira at the market in Onitsha, she uses whole numbers. When you count the number of pupils present in your class, that is whole numbers too. A trader counting bags of garri, a driver counting passengers in a bus, and a farmer counting yams all use whole numbers. They help us share, buy, sell and plan correctly. Numbers are part of our daily life, and the more you practise, the more confident you become. Well done!
